subject: RapidSync POC — activation checklist & peering windows
messages:
From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@rapidsync.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carolyn Simmons <carolyn@rapidsync.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RapidSync POC kickoff — initial infra items

Hi Hannah / Neha,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We want to move the RapidSync evaluation into a short POC (2 weeks) to validate latency and throughput with our ingestion. To get the environment ready we need to align on several items so the engineering teams can start: 

- Org setup: invite two service accounts and a read-only console user for our infra team.
- API keys: one per service account, rotation window of 30 days.
- IP allowlist: we will provide a small set of static egress IPs (attempting to avoid NAT scaling).
- VPC peering: request peering between our production-like VPC and Redwood staging for direct traffic.

Attached is our expected traffic pattern and a basic network diagram. Can you confirm who from your side owns peering and the timeline you typically need? We are aiming to start traffic on Oct 12 and would like a mutual close by Oct 26 if results look good.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Head of Platform Ops
RapidSync

Attachments: rapidsync_traffic_pattern.csv (attachment stub), network_diagram_v2.png (attachment stub)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@rapidsync.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RapidSync POC kickoff — initial infra items

Rajesh — great to see this moving. We can support the Oct 12 start but need to firm up a few details so the MAP and POC run cleanly. Next steps from our side: 

1) Org & API keys
- Please share the preferred email addresses for the two service accounts (we will provision and scope them to the POC org).
- We create API key pairs and can tag them "rs-poc-1" / "rs-poc-2"; keys support a 30-day rotation policy by default.

2) IP allowlist
- Send the exact CIDR blocks you plan to use. We support allowlist at both gateway and instance level; recommend gateway-level for simplicity.

3) VPC peering
- Our networking team requires: VPC IDs, region, account IDs, and a preferred maintenance window for the peering handshake. We typically request a 2-hour window to validate routes.

4) Rollout windows & timeline
- Proposed: peering validated Oct 10–11, keys ready Oct 11, smoke traffic Oct 12 (low-rate), ramp Oct 13–15.
- MAP: mutually agree close criteria (latency < 80ms p95 for your avg request, no more than 2% error rate for 24h).

I attached a short MAP template and a first-draft SOW for your legal team to review.

Hannah
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-rapidmap-v1.pdf (attachment stub), sow-draft-Redwood-RapidSync.docx (attachment stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-05T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RapidSync POC kickoff — initial infra items

Looping in some technical constraints and recommendations for the peering + keys: 

- Peering config
  * We prefer cross-account VPC peering for the POC (no transit gateways) to keep routing simple.
  * Need the exact VPC CIDRs to prevent overlapping (we cannot peer overlapping ranges).
  * Route table updates: one route per subnet we intend to use; please indicate which subnets will carry egress.

- Keys & auth
  * Service accounts should be in format svc-<team>-<env>@rapidsync.ai; we will restrict scopes to the POC org and generation endpoints only.
  * If you plan to use SAML-based user access, let us know for the console read-only user; otherwise we will issue a standard user invite.

- Testing windows
  * Suggest a 30-minute low-traffic smoke test after peering is established, then two 3-hour ramps across separate days to capture diurnal patterns.

If Rajesh can share the VPC IDs and a suggested peering window we will draft the peering ticket for network ops.

—Vivek
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@rapidsync.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-10-07T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RapidSync POC kickoff — initial infra items

Thanks — quick answers inline and payloads attached.

- Service accounts: svc-ingest-poc@rapidsync.ai, svc-qa-poc@rapidsync.ai
- IP/CIDRs: 54.72.128.0/24, 54.72.129.0/24 (these will be our egress NATed IPs)
- VPCs: rs-prod-vpc (vpc-0a1b2c3d) in us-west-2, rs-staging-vpc (vpc-0d3c2b1a) in us-west-2
- Preferred peering window: Oct 10 between 02:00–04:00 UTC (low traffic on our end)

We will also provide a short SAML metadata URL for the console user if you want to configure SSO; otherwise we'll accept a standard invite.

Attachment: rapidsync_vpc_info.json (attachment stub)

Let us know if any of the above collides with your IP ranges or VPC constraints. We can push the peering window by 24 hours if necessary.

—Rajesh

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@rapidsync.ai>, Carolyn Simmons <carolyn@rapidsync.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-11T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RapidSync POC kickoff — initial infra items

Rajesh / Carolyn — all good on our end, thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary and confirmations below so the MAP is explicit and we have clear acceptance criteria and a close timeline.

Summary of actions (owner / ETA):
- Provision service accounts & API keys (Redwood -> hannah_schmitt): keys created and delivered Oct 11 18:00 UTC; tags rs-poc-1 / rs-poc-2.
- VPC peering ticket (Redwood networking -> vivek_kulkarni): peering raised Oct 8, maintenance window scheduled Oct 10 02:00–04:00 UTC.
- IP allowlist (RapidSync -> rajesh): CIDRs received; applied to gateway rules Oct 10 02:15 UTC.
- SSO for console user (RapidSync -> carolyn): we received the SAML metadata and will configure read-only user Oct 11.

POC MAP & close criteria:
- Start smoke traffic Oct 12 03:00 UTC.
- Ramp and observation Oct 13–15.
- Success if: p95 latency < 80ms and sustained error rate < 2% over a 24h window.
- Target mutual close: Oct 26 if success criteria met and both sides sign off on SOW.

Next steps for RapidSync: confirm if you want us to push API keys to your secrets manager (we support AWS Secrets Manager / HashiCorp Vault) or deliver keys via secure DocuSign envelope.

I attached a finalized MAP snapshot and the SOW draft that reflects the agreed timeline. If everything looks good I'll book a 30-minute sync Oct 12 02:30 UTC for the smoke test kickoff.

Thanks — excited to run this with you.

Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-rapidmap-v1.pdf (updated)
